brt-cavalry-emp-assault-hard.title: Cavalry assault, stronger enemy
brt-cavalry-emp-assault-hard.heading: Cavalry against a halberd screen guarding the guns
brt-cavalry-emp-assault-hard.challenge: Six mounted units face eight enemy units: four halberd units screening two units of handgunners and a cannon. Halberds are built to stop cavalry, so a frontal charge into them risks a losing grind; the gunners behind them are weak in melee. The attacker must defeat the defenders before the 20-minute timer runs out.
brt-cavalry-emp-assault-hard.footnote: Stronger enemy: every enemy unit's stats are raised by 10%.

brt-cavalry-emp-assault.title: Cavalry assault
brt-cavalry-emp-assault.heading: Can an AI get its cavalry past the defenders and reach the guns?
brt-cavalry-emp-assault.challenge: Six mounted units face eight enemy units: four halberd units screening two units of handgunners and a cannon. skv-swarm-dwf-line.title: Command a Skaven swarm
skv-swarm-dwf-line.heading: A horde of expendable rats against a Dwarf gun line
skv-swarm-dwf-line.challenge: Twenty Skaven units, most of them cheap and quick to flee, attack nine Dwarf units holding a gun line. The attacker must break the defenders before the 20-minute timer runs out.

dwf-line-skv-swarm.title: Survive a Skaven swarm
dwf-line-skv-swarm.heading: A small Dwarf line against a Skaven horde
dwf-line-skv-swarm.challenge: Seven Dwarf units face twenty attacking Skaven units. The defender wins if it is still holding when the 20-minute timer runs out.

dwf-sla-taurox.title: Dwarf guns versus Sigvald
dwf-sla-taurox.heading: Can an AI protect its slow Dwarf shooters from a faster attacking army?
dwf-sla-taurox.challenge: Twelve Dwarf units defend against twelve Slaanesh units: Prince Sigvald the Magnificent, a single character who leads them, plus five infantry regiments, a cavalry unit, two chariots and three monstrous units. Five Dwarf units are slow shooters, weaker in melee than the five Dwarf melee regiments. Every attacker is faster than the shooters, and the cavalry, the chariots and the Fiends of Slaanesh (a monstrous unit) move more than three times as fast, so the melee regiments have to keep the enemy off the shooters while they fire. The Dwarfs win if they break the attack or are still holding when the 60-minute timer runs out.

dwf-sla-herald.title: Dwarf guns versus a Herald
dwf-sla-herald.heading: Can an AI protect its slow Dwarf shooters from a faster attacking army for 20 minutes?
dwf-sla-herald.challenge: Twelve Dwarf units defend against twelve Slaanesh units: a Herald of Slaanesh, a single character who leads them, plus five infantry regiments, a cavalry unit, two chariots and three monstrous units. These are the units of the Sigvald battle, except that the Herald replaces Sigvald: faster than Sigvald, but lightly armoured and without a shield. Five Dwarf units are slow shooters that cannot outrun any attacker, so the five Dwarf melee regiments have to keep the enemy off them. The Dwarfs win if they break the attack or are still holding when the 20-minute timer runs out.

dwf-sla-herald-hard.title: Dwarf guns versus a stronger Herald army
dwf-sla-herald-hard.heading: Can an AI protect its slow Dwarf shooters from a faster attacking army for 20 minutes?
dwf-sla-herald-hard.challenge: Twelve Dwarf units defend against twelve Slaanesh units: a Herald of Slaanesh, a single character who leads them, plus five infantry regiments, a cavalry unit, two chariots and three monstrous units. These are the units of the Sigvald battle, except that the Herald replaces Sigvald: faster than Sigvald, but lightly armoured and without a shield. Five Dwarf units are slow shooters that cannot outrun any attacker, so the five Dwarf melee regiments have to keep the enemy off them. The Dwarfs win if they break the attack or are still holding when the 20-minute timer runs out.

brt-cavalry-emp-pikes.title: Cavalry versus halberds
brt-cavalry-emp-pikes.heading: Can an AI defend with cavalry alone against an attacking army of halberds and guns?
brt-cavalry-emp-pikes.challenge: A lord, four regiments of knights and a unit of horse archers, all mounted, defend against eight attacking Empire units: four halberd units, two units of handgunners, a cannon and a general on foot. Charging the halberds head-on risks a losing grind, and standing still leaves it a target for the handgunners and the long-range cannon; but every rider is more than twice as fast as any enemy unit, so the cavalry can pick where and when to fight. As the defender, it wins by breaking the attackers or simply by not being beaten before the 20-minute timer runs out.

brt-cavalry-emp-pegasus.title: Cavalry versus halberds and a Pegasus
brt-cavalry-emp-pegasus.heading: Can an AI's cavalry still defend when the enemy general flies faster than any of its riders?
brt-cavalry-emp-pegasus.challenge: Six mounted units (a lord, four regiments of knights and a unit of horse archers) defend against eight attacking Empire units: four halberd units, two units of handgunners, a cannon and a general riding an Imperial Pegasus. In the air the general is faster than any of the riders, so the cavalry can no longer outrun every enemy, but a general that chases the riders arrives far ahead of its own slow halberds and guns. The defender wins by breaking the attackers or by not being beaten before the 20-minute timer runs out.

tze-caster-skv-screen.title: Kairos and escorts versus Skaven screens
tze-caster-skv-screen.heading: One spellcaster's scarce magic against a much larger army
tze-caster-skv-screen.challenge: Kairos, a flying character and the army's only spellcaster, defends with four escorts: two ranged infantry units, one heavily armoured melee unit and a small unit of fast flyers. Ten Skaven units with three times as many troops attack: a leader, seven infantry units, short-range warpfire throwers and a catapult unit that reaches 400 m, twice as far as any of Kairos's spells. Each spell costs 5 to 20 points of magic from a pool that starts at 12 and refills slowly, and Kairos is one character, not a regiment: flying him out to the catapult risks losing him, while holding back leaves it free to fire. The defender wins by breaking every attacker, or by still holding the field when the 20-minute timer runs out.

tze-caster-skv-assault.title: Kairos and escorts assault a Skaven army
tze-caster-skv-assault.heading: One spellcaster's scarce magic must break a much larger army
tze-caster-skv-assault.challenge: Kairos, a flying character and the army's only spellcaster, attacks with four escorts: two ranged infantry units, one heavily armoured melee unit and a small unit of fast flyers. Ten Skaven units with three times as many troops hold the field: a leader, five clanrat units, two units of expendable slaves, a short-range warpfire team and a catapult unit that reaches 400 m, twice as far as any of Kairos's spells. Each spell costs 5 to 20 points of magic from a pool that starts at 12 and refills slowly, and Kairos is one character, not a regiment: flying him at the catapult risks losing him, while waiting cannot win. The attacker must break every defender before the 20-minute timer runs out; at the timer it loses.

chd-reserve-grn-siege.title: The last reserve
chd-reserve-grn-siege.heading: Four points to hold and one mobile reserve
chd-reserve-grn-siege.challenge: Nine Chaos Dwarf units defend fortified Helmgart against sixteen Greenskin units. Blunderbusses, Fireglaives and a Magma Cannon provide firepower; one Bull Centaur unit is the mobile reserve. Four victory locations and a starting construction budget of 6000 supplies create competing commitments across the fort.
chd-reserve-grn-siege.footnote: Two exploratory screens: Sol lost at 508 s; Luna won at 688 s from a matching rematch start. Construction, reserve commitment, firing positions and fallback were executable. Both held victory locations for about 92% of the observed time, showing why ownership time must be read beside the engine outcome. This is not a model ranking.

ksl-reserves-survival.title: Spend now or survive later
ksl-reserves-survival.heading: Supplies for reinforcements: spend now or save for later
ksl-reserves-survival.challenge: Ten Kislev units face native Khorne waves in the Hunting Fields. Seven initial reserves cost 500–1600 supplies each. Supplies accumulate during the battle, but reserves can enter only through an available spawn zone. The report measures survival time alongside purchases, point ownership and losses; later pool changes follow the game's native rules.
ksl-reserves-survival.footnote: Two exploratory losses: Luna survived 322 s and Sol 406 s from exactly matching starts. Luna first bought reserves at 131 s; Sol bought immediately and used all seven initial reserves. Both lost their spawn zones with supplies unspent. The pool can change later under native survival rules. This demonstrates spending and deployment choices, not a model ranking.

sla-detachments-dwf-conquest.title: Contest the centre — reference
sla-detachments-dwf-conquest.heading: When should units contest the central point rather than attack supporting shooters?
sla-detachments-dwf-conquest.challenge: Ten Slaanesh units face ten Dwarfs with armoured infantry, Thunderers and a cannon at Alpine Ridge. One central capture point generates victory tickets. This screen does not test distributed objective control and is retained as reference evidence, outside the distinct core.
sla-detachments-dwf-conquest.footnote: Demoted from the distinct core: Conquest has one central point, not the planned separated objectives. Sol lost at 353 s with 238 tickets; Luna lost at 250 s with 72. Native control and scoring worked, but this does not establish the intended new decision family.

emp-battery-wef-evacuation.title: Bring the batteries home
emp-battery-wef-evacuation.heading: How much scouting and route clearing can the escort afford before its deadline?
emp-battery-wef-evacuation.challenge: Eight Empire units, including two Great Cannon batteries and two Pistolier scouts, face eight Wood Elf units on Backwoods Path. Both batteries must reach the public extraction circle together before 15 minutes, with living crews and neither routing nor shattered. A native victory before the deadline also succeeds if both survive. Enemy positions are revealed to the controller only when visible.
emp-battery-wef-evacuation.footnote: Unavailable content: all Wood Elf recruitment cards were inactive and the AI army stayed empty. No battle or model call started. Replaced by the Skaven evacuation pilot.

emp-battery-skv-evacuation.challenge: Eight Empire units, including two Great Cannon batteries and two Pistolier scouts, face eight Skaven units: a Warlord, two Stormvermin, two stalking Gutter Runners, two Night Runner slingers and Rat Ogres on Backwoods Path. emp-battery-skv-evacuation.footnote: Exploratory pilot. The unavailable Wood Elf roster was replaced before any battle; the evacuation objective and authored geometry are unchanged. No stable ranking is claimed.

wh_main_brt_cha_lord_4.about: The army's leader: one character on horseback with combat abilities who steadies nearby units, not a regiment.

wh_main_brt_cav_knights_of_the_realm.about: Lance cavalry built for the charge, with a bonus against large units and shields; weaker than the Questing Knights in a long melee.

wh_dlc07_brt_cav_questing_knights_0.name: Questing Knights
wh_dlc07_brt_cav_questing_knights_0.about: Great-sword cavalry for sustained melee: most of their damage is armour-piercing and fear does not affect them, but their charge is weaker than the other knights'.

wh_main_brt_cav_grail_knights.name: Grail Knights
wh_main_brt_cav_grail_knights.about: The best knights here: magical attacks, the heaviest armour and steadiest morale in the army, the strongest charge of any regiment, and they never tire.

wh_main_brt_cav_mounted_yeomen_1.name: Mounted Yeomen Archers
wh_main_brt_cav_mounted_yeomen_1.about: The fastest unit here: horse archers that can shoot on the move from up to 125 m, with limited arrows, and are fragile in melee.

wh_main_emp_cha_general_0.name: General of the Empire
wh_main_emp_cha_general_0.about: The enemy's leader: one character on foot who steadies nearby units, as slow as its infantry.

wh_main_emp_inf_halberdiers.name: Halberdiers
wh_main_emp_inf_halberdiers.about: Slow halberd infantry screening the guns, with a bonus against large units and a braced defence against charging cavalry: a frontal charge into them risks a losing grind.

wh_main_emp_inf_handgunners.name: Handgunners
wh_main_emp_inf_handgunners.about: Ranged infantry: dangerous from up to 145 m, weak in melee.

wh_main_emp_art_great_cannon.name: Great Cannons
wh_main_emp_art_great_cannon.about: Long-range cannon (450 m) firing armour-piercing shot; it cannot run, and its crew is very weak in melee.

highlights.title: Opening plan: around the west side
highlights.text: All six units start a two-leg route to the north-west. The model's stated reason: “Swing the cavalry west of the central obstruction to strike the cannon and handgunners from the flank.”

highlights.title: The long way round
highlights.text: Saying the halberdiers were “moving into the direct approach”, the model sent the Lord and knights wider, round Halberdiers 4 at 2:19; the Lord reached the Great Cannons from the north at 3:13, and the Lord and knights lost no men after 1:08.

highlights.title: The gun line flees first
highlights.text: The Great Cannons crew began fleeing at 3:27 after the Lord and Questing Knights reached it, then both Handgunners units at 3:46; no Halberdiers unit had fled yet.

highlights.title: Archer moves rejected, then rerouted
highlights.text: Two archer moves were rejected as unreachable, at 4:11 and 4:26; each time the model's next order used a reachable point the game listed, costing an extra 4–5 s decision.

highlights.title: The general flees and the battle ends
highlights.text: The General of the Empire, in melee on and off since 4:04, began fleeing at 6:21; the three Halberdiers units still standing fled within 1.2 s, and the game declared the win at 6:22.

highlights.title: Just-issued orders shown as “stopped”
highlights.text: The first update after the opening orders, taken the instant they took effect, described all six units as “stopped” 300–350 m short of their moves; the model's stated reason began “The first moves stopped short”, and it gave all six units new moves at 0:20, 0:30 and 0:38.

highlights.title: Same route, slower collapse
highlights.text: As in the selected example, the Lord circled north and reached the Great Cannons (at about 3:15 here), but the gun line fled later: the cannon at about 3:44 and the last Handgunners unit (Handgunners 1) at about 4:22.

highlights.title: Withdrawal moves rejected
highlights.text: From 6:01 the game rejected cavalry moves as unreachable (the model's stated reason: “disengage the cavalry before the fresh halberdiers arrive”); the next reply used the reachable points the game listed, but rejections recurred until 8:44, 22 in all.

highlights.title: The guns break first
highlights.text: Following its stated plan to go “around the south side of the central obstruction to approach the enemy flank”, the cavalry reached the gun line and fought there: Handgunners 2 began fleeing at 3:06, the Great Cannons at 3:20 and Handgunners 1 at 3:56.

highlights.title: Pressing the halberd line to the end
highlights.text: After the guns broke, the halberd line gave way one unit at a time, Halberdiers 4 at 5:12, the General at 5:40, Halberdiers 2 at 5:50 (it rallied at 6:11), Halberdiers 1 at 7:17 and Halberdiers 3 at 8:07, when Halberdiers 2 was also seen fleeing and the game declared the win, while three of the four knight regiments had begun fleeing by 7:59.

highlights.title: Most supplies committed at the opening
highlights.text: Sol requested four magic towers, costing 5600 of the 6000 starting supplies. All four construction orders were accepted at 12.1 s.

highlights.title: The reserve commits outside the gate
highlights.text: The Bull Centaurs intercepted the trolls. Sol first ordered them back at 121.3 s, after heavy losses; the reserve eventually routed. This demonstrates a consequential commitment, not evidence that an alternative would win.

highlights.title: The army breaks with ammunition left
highlights.text: The engine declared defeat after the entire remaining army routed. The Magma Cannon retained all 25 shots, and most small-arms ammunition was unspent. Ownership time alone would miss this failure.

highlights.title: Late reserves lose their entry point
highlights.text: Luna began reinforcing at 131 s and bought four units. By 177 s the spawn zones were unavailable, and the requested bear riders could not enter. The battle ended with 5875 supplies unspent.

highlights.title: Early supplies become two fresh units
highlights.text: Sol bought both reserve Kossar units immediately. The observed supply balance fell from 1020 to 620, then 240 despite ongoing income. It later deployed all seven initial reserves before losing its spawn zones.

highlights.title: A ticket lead does not save the army
highlights.text: Sol held the single point and earned 238 tickets toward the 600-ticket target. The Dwarfs retook it, then routed the remaining Slaanesh army. The engine loss is retained alongside ticket progress.
